title: Jaishankar Meets Ras Al Khaimah Ruler on Final Day of UAE Visit
excerpt: The external affairs minister's talks with Sheikh Saud bin Saqr Al Qasimi covered India-UAE ties and the Gulf situation, closing a three-day visit built around the Raisina Middle East Dialogue.
body:
• External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Sheikh Saud bin Saqr Al Qasimi, Ruler of Ras Al Khaimah and a member of the UAE Supreme Council, in Abu Dhabi on Friday.
  • The talks covered strengthening India-UAE ties, deeper regional engagement and the current situation in the Gulf.
  • The meeting closed a three-day visit from October 14 to 16 that included the Raisina Middle East Dialogue and talks with UAE Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
  • India and the UAE are linked by a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and bilateral trade estimated at more than $85 billion.

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Sheikh Saud bin Saqr Al Qasimi, the Ruler of Ras Al Khaimah, in Abu Dhabi on Friday, on the final day of a three-day visit to the United Arab Emirates. The discussions focused on strengthening India-UAE ties and on the situation in the Gulf, according to Jaishankar and reports of the meeting.

Ras Al Khaimah is the northernmost of the seven emirates and sits along the Gulf coast near the Strait of Hormuz. Its ruler is also a member of the UAE Supreme Council, the federation's highest authority, which placed the meeting at the top tier of the UAE's federal structure rather than at the level of a single emirate.

"An honour to meet HH Sheikh Saud bin Saqr Al Qasimi, the Ruler of Ras Al Khaimah and member of the UAE Supreme Council."

— S. Jaishankar, External Affairs Minister

A Visit Built Around the Raisina Dialogue

Jaishankar arrived in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday. On October 14 he met his UAE counterpart, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, for talks on bilateral and global issues held, in his words, in the spirit of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

On October 15 he took part in the Raisina Middle East Dialogue, a forum co-hosted by India's Ministry of External Affairs and the UAE foreign ministry. Speaking in a session on continental corridors, he argued that competition has intensified, new chokepoints have emerged and globalisation must be navigated with greater resilience. He said the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor, known as IMEC, is already shaping regional thinking on connectivity, and that India is building its own strengths while establishing trusted partnerships.

Why the Gulf Conversation Matters

The Gulf discussion in the Ras Al Khaimah meeting was not a formality. The region remains a focal point of geopolitical attention amid ongoing tensions, and shipping and energy routes through and near the Strait of Hormuz carry direct consequences for India, a large energy importer.

The partnership Jaishankar was reviewing has widened well beyond energy. Formalised as a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2017, it now covers trade, investment, defence and security. The Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, in force since May 2022, set the trade framework, and bilateral trade has been estimated at more than $85 billion, making the UAE one of India's largest trading partners.

The Diaspora Stake

For Indians abroad, the relationship is personal as well as diplomatic. The Gulf is home to millions of Indian workers and professionals, including a large community in the UAE itself, whose remittances, jobs and safety depend on stable ties between New Delhi and Abu Dhabi. High-level visits that include emirate-level rulers, not only federal ministers, widen the channels available when consular, labour or investment issues arise in a specific emirate such as Ras Al Khaimah.

What Comes Next

Jaishankar's October 14-16 visit combined a multilateral dialogue with a sequence of bilateral meetings, a pattern Indian officials have used to keep Gulf engagement active across several tracks at once. With the visit concluded, attention turns to follow-through on the partnership agenda discussed in Abu Dhabi, and to how the corridor and connectivity ideas aired at the Raisina dialogue translate into projects through the remainder of 2026.
